summary: Closed the measured B411 launcher-loss gap (request d6b6e8ee4080420fb555692e741452bf exited successfully at 2026-07-15T14:21:41Z but stayed processing until a coordinator manually invoked reconciliation at 15:21Z). Root cause: ProcessManager only re-scans persisted requests when a NEW instance happens to be constructed (MCP server restart or an explicit status/list/reconcile call) -- nothing re-scans on its own between those events. Added a token-free supervisor heartbeat (worker_supervisor.py::supervise): every heartbeat_interval_seconds (default 15s, configurable per-spec for tests) the supervisor atomically refreshes its existing owner-only 0600 status artifact with a monotonic heartbeat_seq, heartbeat_at_epoch, supervisor_pid+supervisor_pid_start_ticks, child_pid+child_pid_start_ticks, stdout_bytes/stderr_bytes, and last_output_change_epoch -- fully independent of task lifecycle/updated_at and of any model/dashboard/MCP turn. Added process_launcher.py::derive_liveness_state, a pure function deriving alive/quiet/unresponsive/lost from heartbeat age, activity age, and exact PID+start-tick identity (never from bare process existence): alive = fresh heartbeat + exact identity; quiet = alive but output unchanged beyond a configurable warning interval (never a failure); unresponsive = heartbeat lease expired while the exact process still exists; lost = exact PID identity gone, or an unresponsive supervisor exceeded the bounded recovery grace. Added process_launcher.py::read_supervisor_status, a hardened reader that fails closed (returns {}) on a symlink, non-regular file, foreign owner, or insecure permission bits. Wired derive_liveness_state into ProcessManager._finalize_isolated_request: when a supervisor's heartbeat lease AND recovery grace both elapse while its exact PID still exists, the request is escalated to 'lost', identity is rechecked once more under the registry lock immediately before any action, and ONLY the exact matching supervisor/child process group(s) are terminated (never a bare-PID kill) before finalizing as worker_failed -- never pending, never automatic retry. Added tools/aiworkhub/src/aiworkhub/task_reconciler.py: an idempotent, provider-neutral CLI/daemon (run-once/daemon/status) with a 30s default scan interval (AIWORKHUB_RECONCILER_SCAN_INTERVAL_SECONDS) and a single-instance flock-based advisory lock, separate from ProcessManager's own interprocess-safe _registry_lock. It introduces NO second task queue and NO duplicate promotion logic -- run_scan()/run_daemon() only repeatedly call the EXISTING ProcessManager.reconcile() (== _reconcile_persisted_requests -> _finalize_isolated_request), so a successfully exited worker is reconciled through the unchanged scope-validate-promote-review path even after the launching MCP/VS Code/launcker process is gone, and a lost/timed-out/cancelled/failed worker is routed to review/blocked with a normalized outcome, never silently to pending. Extended dashboard.py: read_process_runs() now reads the owner-only supervisor heartbeat file (bounded, server-side only -- the raw status path itself is never exposed to the browser, matching the existing stdout_path/stderr_path exclusion policy) and attaches derived liveness_state/heartbeat_age_seconds/activity_age_seconds/supervisor_alive/child_alive/runtime_seconds/last_activity_at to each process row; build_snapshot() merges these (plus model) onto the owning task row without touching dashboard_static/*.js -- dashboard.js already renders task.updated_at || task.last_activity_at for the Activity column, so the task table now shows a real timestamp instead of Unknown for any task driven by a live isolated worker. Added a repo-local, NOT-installed systemd --user unit template (scripts/geoai-task-reconciler.service) and a geoai-task-reconciler console-script entry point (pyproject.toml) for Codex to apply after review.

environment_note.chmod_fchmod_syscall_blocked_in_this_san: Independently reproduces the identical restriction documented in eval/task_mcp_vscode_owned_app_server_mux_b409_v1.json: a bare os.chmod()/os.fchmod()/Path.chmod() call fails with PermissionError('Operation not permitted') in this worker's sandboxed shell, including on paths/fds this same process just created and owns, and including with dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true (confirmed via a direct probe). os.mkdir(mode=)/os.open(mode=) still apply permission bits correctly at creation time. Worked around for in-process test execution ONLY via a probe-based autouse pytest fixture (_bridge_chmod_sandbox_restriction, added to all three required test files) that monkeypatches os.chmod/os.fchmod to a no-op EXCLUSIVELY when a one-time probe proves the syscall is genuinely blocked -- a host where chmod works exercises the real, unmodified permission-setting code path. This CANNOT bridge a separate subprocess's own internal chmod calls (e.g. the real `git` binary invoked by test_process_launcher_security.py's `repo` fixture), which is why that file's five git-worktree-dependent tests remain unrunnable here specifically (not a B412 regression).
